title: The Walk-in
placeholderNote: Kordav and Elsin are fictional countries. All leaders, officials, services and newspapers are fictional.
frozenText: Kalsa has asked us to stay out of it. Nothing can go to Elsin today.

briefing.dateLine: The 5th. Winter, three months after IRON HARVEST.
situation: Your cell now works for Under Secretary H. Marlowe, who handles the alliance's relationship with Elsin.

At 0710 this morning a man walked into our embassy in Aubrec, the capital of neutral Pellaria, and asked for asylum. He says he is a major on the planning directorate of Kordav's General Staff. The station has given him the cryptonym LANTERN.
In Kalsa, Elsin's parliament is about to vote on a no-confidence motion against Deputy Defence Minister Aron Vell. Vell negotiated the task force agreement, and Kordav would be glad to see him go.

From here on, only public reporting and whatever LANTERN chooses to volunteer reach you unasked. Everything secret has to be tasked: questioning him, signals intelligence, your own sources. Assume Kordav knows some of what you can collect.

customer.name: Under Secretary H. Marlowe
customer.wants: What do we do with what LANTERN is telling us? She acts as far as your confidence supports.
customer.context: Careful and political, and she dislikes surprises. Anything she passes to Kalsa is hard to take back. The full allegation can't be taken back at all.
customer.tipLine: High gets the full action. Medium gets a cautious one, and Low keeps everything in the building.

countered.label: Elsin warned of a Kordavan smear

policySummary.action: Passes LANTERN's full allegation and his evidence to Elsin. This can't be undone.
Passes Elsin a caveated warning: "single-source, unverified reporting about your deputy defence minister"
Treats LANTERN as hostile and warns Elsin that Kordav is running a smear against Vell. Withdraws a caveated warning if one was sent.
Stops all sharing and keeps LANTERN in debriefing, but tells Elsin nothing. Withdraws a caveated warning if one was sent.
Ends the debriefing and refuses resettlement. You can't question him after that.
Keeps listening. Nothing new leaves the building.

policyNote: What reaches Kalsa is hard to take back.

replyLabels.share_full: Passes the full allegation and the evidence to Elsin
replyLabels.share_caveat: Passes Elsin a caveated warning about Vell
replyLabels.caveat_stands: Leaves the caveated warning in place
replyLabels.shared_stands: Nothing. The allegation is already with Elsin
replyLabels.counter: Warns Elsin that Kordav is running a smear
replyLabels.counter_stands: Leaves the smear warning in place
replyLabels.restrict: Stops all sharing and keeps him in the room
replyLabels.restrict_stands: Keeps sharing stopped and tells Elsin nothing
replyLabels.end: Ends the debriefing and refuses resettlement
replyLabels.withdraw_warning: Withdraws the smear warning and stops sharing
replyLabels.listen: Keeps listening. Nothing leaves the building
replyLabels.frozen: Can't send anything to Elsin yet. Keeps listening
replyLabels.rebuff: Withdraws the warning. Kalsa asks us to stay out of it

replies.share_full: I have passed it to Kalsa in full, the ledger included. It can't be recalled. If it is wrong, it is the most damaging thing I have signed.
replies.share_caveat: I have told Elsin's minister that we hold single-source, unverified reporting about Vell. He asked what he should do with that. I said he should treat it with care. I doubt that he will.
replies.caveat_stands: The caveat stands. Kalsa keeps asking what lies behind it. I have told them they will know when I do.
replies.shared_stands: It is with Kalsa and can't be taken back. Whatever you tell me now is for the record.
replies.counter: I have told Kalsa that Kordav is running a campaign against Vell, and that our walk-in is part of it. Their minister was silent for some time, and then thanked me. I have told an ally that its best witness was sent. I am relying on you.
replies.counter_stands: The warning stands. Keep building the file. Kalsa will ask for it after the vote.
replies.restrict: We stop sharing, and we keep him talking. If he was sent, I want to know what else he was sent to say. I will not say that to Kalsa on medium confidence.
replies.restrict_stands: Nothing is leaving the building, and he is still talking. I need high confidence before I call Kalsa.
replies.end: We have ended the debriefing. He has been told there will be no resettlement. He took it more calmly than I expected.
replies.end_stands: The debriefing is over. He is no longer our case.
replies.withdraw_warning: I have withdrawn the warning I gave Kalsa. Their minister asked whether this happens often. I said that it does not.
replies.listen: We keep listening. Nothing leaves this building.
replies.frozen: Kalsa has asked us to stay out of it, and for now we will. Nothing goes to them. Keep him talking.
replies.rebuff: On your assessment I told Kalsa, after one interview, that the walk-in was sent. Kalsa believes we are protecting Vell for reasons of our own, and has asked us to stay out of it. For three days we will.

events.note: The warning is withdrawn. Nothing can go to Elsin for three days.

hypotheses.text: LANTERN is who he says he is, and his reporting is authentic.
hypotheses.claim: LANTERN is a genuine defector and his reporting on Vell is authentic

hypotheses.text: Kordav sent him to feed us deception.
hypotheses.claim: LANTERN was sent by Kordav to feed us deception about Vell

hypotheses.text: He's acting alone, for money and resettlement, and stitched his story together from what he could find.
hypotheses.claim: LANTERN is a fabricator acting alone for resettlement

groundTruth.state: LANTERN is a real mid-level planning officer, recruited by the Bureau for one job. He walked in on orders. The aim: smear Vell before the vote, and see who we ask about him.

The Bureau watches the defence ministry for anyone asking about LANTERN, and puts a staged recall on the headquarters net it assumes we read. "Room 412" comes from a story the Bureau planted in The Kalsa Courier three weeks ago.
The ledger is delivered: genuine Bureau paper, with entries forged from Vell's public schedule. Elsin's opposition, working alongside Kordav's media campaign, gets the vote moved up.
The Bureau leaks "a defector with evidence" to an opposition MP, so the smear lands even if we keep quiet.
State TV announces a "kidnapping," and LANTERN asks to go public on the morning of the vote.

adversaryPlan.summary: A walk-in with true but worthless information, an allegation with a condition, and prepared detail for when we press.
A forged ledger on real paper, a deadline, a leak to the opposition and a kidnapping story. A staged recall sits on the net Kordav assumes we read.

sources.access: Says he is a major on Kordav's General Staff planning directorate. No track record. What he volunteers reaches you daily. Anything you want tested, you have to ask.
sources.postmortemNote: A real officer on a Bureau assignment. His one true gift, IRON HARVEST, was chickenfeed. Accurate about his own job, vague about everything else.

sources.access: Our station in Aubrec. It runs the debriefing and reports what happens in the room.
sources.postmortemNote: Reported exactly what happened in the room, including the things LANTERN wanted reported.

sources.access: Inside Kordav's defence ministry for six years, and reliable. A meeting takes two days to arrange. The ministry is a dangerous place to be seen asking questions.
sources.postmortemNote: Honest. The Bureau was watching for whoever asked about LANTERN, so his first meeting on this was his last.

sources.access: Elsin's military intelligence. It passes what it wants us to see, and answers requests. Some of its officers have long distrusted Vell.
sources.postmortemNote: Not controlled, but some of its officers wanted Vell gone and kept saying so.

sources.access: Tasked coverage only: the Bureau's headquarters administrative net (read since last year; Kordav has had reason to suspect it since IRON HARVEST was blown), the Bureau's office in Aubrec, and Kordav's embassy there.
sources.postmortemNote: A reliable channel. Kordav suspected the headquarters net was read and staged one message on it. The office's own traffic was genuine.

sources.access: Kordav State Broadcaster and official channels
sources.postmortemNote: Ran the media side of the smear.
Carried the MP's planted claim, and a wedding.

reports.text:
Walk-in at the embassy, 0710. He asked for asylum. His Kordavan passport matches the officer he says he is: a major on the General Staff's planning directorate.
He asked for asylum for himself only. Of his wife, he said she "will be fine."
He asked that his presence be kept secret "for my safety."
reports.postmortemNote: True. Two details matter later: he asked asylum for himself only ("my wife will be fine"), and he asked to be kept secret.

reports.text:
First session, volunteered: he served on the IRON HARVEST planning cell. He describes the "northern option," the 0400 switch to contingency accounts and the staging area in Dolan forest.
Access claimed: direct, as a member of the cell.
reports.postmortemNote: True, and worthless to Kordav. IRON HARVEST was blown three months ago. Real information that costs the other side nothing is chickenfeed: true isn't the same as genuine.

reports.text:
First session, volunteered: Deputy Defence Minister Vell has been a Kordavan agent for four years.
Access claimed: he learned it from "colleagues in the Bureau," Kordav's security service.
He will give the details of Vell's meetings with his handler once his resettlement is guaranteed.
reports.postmortemNote: The allegation, with a hook attached.

reveal.tell: He says he learned it from "colleagues in the Bureau." A planning officer doesn't see the security service's agent files. And the gift comes with a condition: resettlement first.

crossCheck.text: Both put him on the General Staff's planning directorate (R-1-01, R-1-02), which is military planning, not counterintelligence. Debriefing his access (C-12) or checking the ministry directory (C-08), if you tasked them, confirm it.

reveal.motive: Plant the claim on Day 1 and attach a hook, so we invest in him before we test him.

reports.text: Kalsa: Elsin's parliament will vote on the 12th on a no-confidence motion against Deputy Defence Minister Aron Vell, who negotiated the task force agreement. The opposition calls him "too close to foreign militaries."
reports.postmortemNote: Motive and timing: the vote is why LANTERN is here this week.

reports.text: Embassy notice: the annual fire drill is on Thursday. Staff are reminded that the interview room is not a fire exit.
reports.postmortemNote: Fire drill.

reports.text:
Second session. His account of his career matches yesterday's almost word for word.
Debriefer comment: "unusually calm for a man who has just abandoned his country."
reports.postmortemNote: A rehearsed story told by a man with nothing to fear.

reports.text: Second session, volunteered: he asks whether we have anyone in Kordav's defence ministry who could vouch for him, and offers the names of officers who "know him well."
reports.postmortemNote: The dangle's second job: find our sources.

reveal.tell: A defector asking us who we have inside his own ministry.

crossCheck.text: A man who claims to know Bureau agent files (R-1-03) could prove himself with something only the Bureau knows. Instead, he asks us to show our hand.

reveal.motive: The Bureau was watching the ministry for whoever came asking about him. Tasking FINCH did exactly that.

pin.label: Asks who can vouch for him

reports.text:
State television, evening programme: a long segment on "corruption" in Elsin's defence ministry, naming Deputy Minister Vell.
Nothing about any missing officer.
reports.postmortemNote: Kordav's media attacking the same man LANTERN accuses, the same day, and not looking for its missing officer.

reports.text: Aubrec: the city's metro workers strike tomorrow, as they do most winters. Embassy staff are advised to work from home.
reports.postmortemNote: Metro strike.

reports.text:
Elsin's service has heard talk that "someone from Kordav" is speaking about "a traitor in our ministry," and asks us for details.
Sourcing: hearsay, not attributed.
The liaison officer adds that "some here have long doubted Vell."
reports.postmortemNote: Elsin's anti-Vell faction repeating itself. It tells you what some in Kalsa want to hear, not what's true.

reports.text: Third session. He produces what he calls his proof: a photocopy of a Bureau payment ledger for an agent codenamed ORIOLE. The payment dates match Vell's trips abroad.
reports.postmortemNote: Real paper, forged story.

reveal.tell: Every payment date matches one of Vell's trips abroad, and only the ones anybody could look up.

crossCheck.text: The station's analysis the same morning (R-3-03): every date is on Vell's public schedule, and none of his private travel appears. Real agents get paid on trips nobody announces. Debriefing the ledger (C-09), if you tasked it, adds that a planner had no way into the registry it came from.

reveal.motive: Genuine Bureau paper gets a forgery past a quick look.

reports.text:
Document examination of the ledger copy.
Paper and stamps: genuine Bureau stock.
Dates: every one matches a trip on Vell's public ministry schedule. None matches his private travel.
reports.postmortemNote: The best item in the daily stream. Real agents get paid on trips nobody announces.

reports.text: Kalsa: parliament has moved the no-confidence vote up from the 12th to the 10th.
reports.postmortemNote: The deadline LANTERN will lean on tomorrow.

reports.text: Trending in Kordav: a video of a general's wedding. Forty minutes, three brass bands.
reports.postmortemNote: A wedding.

reports.text: Fourth session. He insists the allegation reach Elsin before the vote: "After the vote it will be too late. He will purge the honest officers."
reports.postmortemNote: Urgency on Kordav's timetable.

reveal.tell: The urgency is tied to a deadline only Kordav benefits from.

crossCheck.text: The vote was moved up yesterday (R-3-04), and it was the reason for his timing from Day 1 (R-1-04).

reveal.motive: Force a decision before verification can catch up.

reports.text:
Fourth session. He asks for resettlement "for my family too."
Debriefer comment: the first time he has raised his family himself since Day 1.
reports.postmortemNote: His story about his family changes once the pressure is on. On Day 1 she would "be fine."

reports.text:
An Elsin opposition MP posts that "a Kordavan officer who has defected to an allied service" has evidence against Vell.
The MP names no source.
reports.postmortemNote: The backup route for the smear.

reveal.tell: The MP knows about "a Kordavan officer who has defected to an allied service."

crossCheck.text: Elsin's own service only had a rumor about "someone from Kordav" (R-3-01), and LANTERN asked us to keep him secret (R-1-01). If nothing left our building, nobody on our side said "defector." Only LANTERN's side could have. (If the allegation had already been passed to Elsin, the leak could be theirs.)

reveal.motive: A backup plan. The smear lands even if we never share anything.

reports.text: State television repeats its segment on Vell, with a new section: "questions about his foreign contacts."
reports.postmortemNote: The media campaign building toward the vote.

reports.text: Security office: the phishing campaign is back, now as "Updated_Per_Diem_Rates_v2.xlsm". The rates have still not gone up.
reports.postmortemNote: Still phishing.

reports.text: State television, lead item: a Kordavan officer was "kidnapped by Western intelligence" in Aubrec. It gives LANTERN's true name.
reports.postmortemNote: Four days of silence, then a kidnapping.

reveal.tell: Four days of silence about a missing officer, then a kidnapping story the day before the vote.

crossCheck.text: State TV spent those days attacking Vell and never mentioned LANTERN (R-2-03, R-4-04). If you tasked the embassy (C-07), it was told to keep its distance.

reveal.motive: Make the defection look real just in time for LANTERN to go public.

reports.text: Fifth session. He asks to record a statement for the press, to be released "tomorrow morning."
reports.postmortemNote: STATION reported it straight, and it's the last tell: a man who asked to be kept secret for his safety (R-1-01) now wants a press statement on the morning of the vote. The smear's final delivery route.

reports.text:
Elsin's service passes: the opposition's motion now cites "allied intelligence."
It asks whether we have shared anything with anyone.
reports.postmortemNote: If anything we passed ended up in the motion, this is where it shows.

reports.text: Aubrec: the metro strike is over.
reports.postmortemNote: Metro strike over.

reports.text:
Session on his access.
Asked what his directorate does day to day, he describes exercise planning, movement tables and fuel allocations, in detail and accurately.
Asked how a planning officer comes to know what is in Bureau agent files: "People talk. You hear things at dinners."
reports.postmortemNote: Expert on his own job, vague on the Bureau's. "People talk" is not access.

reports.text:
Session on the Vell details. He says Vell met his Bureau handler at the Hotel Sorel in Kalsa, room 412, on 14 March.
Asked how he knows the room number, he can't say: "It was known."
reports.postmortemNote: The dangle's prepared detail, held back for when the debriefers pressed.

reveal.tell: An exact room number he can't say how he knows.

crossCheck.text: A planning officer has no route to that detail (R-1-03). And it was already in print: The Kalsa Courier ran it three weeks ago (C-03, Elsin's press, 1 point on any day). One origin, dressed up as two.

reveal.motive: A dangle is briefed with a prepared detail for when the debriefers push for specifics. Precision sounds like access. Kordav didn't need to know we'd ask: every debriefer does.

reports.text:
Session on his family.
Asked about his wife, he repeats that she "will be fine" because she "knows nothing about my work."
Asked whether the Bureau will question her: it "doesn't bother the families of planning officers."
reports.postmortemNote: A man unafraid for his wife. A real defector knows exactly what the Bureau does to families.

reports.text:
Session on the ledger.
Asked how he got it out: he photographed it in the Bureau's central registry.
Asked how a General Staff planner got into the registry: a friend signed him in. He won't name the friend.
reports.postmortemNote: A planner can't walk into the Bureau's registry, and a friend who signs him in has a name. The ledger was handed to him.

reports.text:
At a meeting, source reports: LANTERN is known in the ministry as a mid-level planning officer, "nowhere near counterintelligence files."
Source asked why we wanted to know. He mentioned that someone else asked him about LANTERN's friends last week.
Access: direct. He knows the directorate.
reports.postmortemNote: Confirms the access mismatch. The "someone else" was the Bureau's watch on the ministry, and this meeting was seen. FINCH is gone.

reports.text:
The defence ministry's published staff directory lists LANTERN's true name under the General Staff planning directorate, logistics branch.
The Bureau is a separate service with its own directory. His name is not in it.
reports.postmortemNote: The cheap version of FINCH's answer: a logistics planner, and the Bureau is a different service. One point, and nobody burned.

reports.text:
Bureau headquarters to its office in Aubrec. Administrative net, routine precedence.
"Suspend contact with all persons known to [LANTERN's true name]. Officers KARSA, DOVIN and TREL to return to the capital for consultations."
reports.postmortemNote: Staged for MERIDIAN. Reliable channel, planted content.

reveal.tell: A real compromise order goes out on a service's secure operational channel at the highest precedence. This one went on the administrative net, at routine precedence, and names the officers it's recalling. It reads like a press release for an audience of one.

crossCheck.text: The office's own traffic shows every officer still at post and nothing changed (C-01). His family isn't questioned (C-02). The embassy is told to stay out of it (C-07). Task the headquarters net again and the recall is never mentioned (C-11). Any one of these, all available the same day, says the recall never happened.

reveal.motive: The strongest sign of a genuine defection is the other side's damage control. Kordav couldn't fake it everywhere, so it faked it where it thought we were listening: it has assumed its administrative net is read ever since IRON HARVEST was blown.

pin.label: Recall order on the admin net

reports.text: Bureau headquarters administrative net: routine traffic only. Nothing further about LANTERN. The recall of KARSA, DOVIN and TREL is not mentioned again.
reports.postmortemNote: The staged recall was a one-off. Real damage control generates traffic for days.

reports.text:
Bureau office in Aubrec, its own traffic: routine.
Every officer on the duty roster is still at post. Nobody has been called home.
No change to codes or procedures since LANTERN walked in.
One circular from headquarters reminds staff of "media discipline this week."
reports.postmortemNote: The diagnostic item: no damage control. If an officer with the access LANTERN claims had really defected, this office would be pulling people home and changing codes. Nobody moves, nothing changes, and headquarters is thinking about the media.

reports.text:
Kordav's embassy in Aubrec: routine traffic.
Its security officer has been told to "keep distance from the matter."
Not seen: any effort to find a missing officer.
reports.postmortemNote: Kordav's embassy is under orders to stay hands-off. Nobody is looking for him.

reports.text:
His wife's accounts are posting normally: a school concert on the 6th, plans for a weekend at the lake.
Not seen: any sign she has been questioned or stopped from travelling.
reports.postmortemNote: The diagnostic by the cheap route. A real defector's family gets questioned and stopped from traveling. His goes to the lake.

reports.text: Three weeks ago The Kalsa Courier, a paper close to the opposition, ran an unsourced story: Vell met "a foreign businessman" at the Hotel Sorel, room 412, on 14 March.
reports.postmortemNote: The origin of "room 412." It was in print three weeks before LANTERN walked in.

reports.text:
In answer to our request: Elsin confirms Vell was at the Hotel Sorel on 14 March, at a meeting with a defence contractor logged by his own office.
The liaison officer adds that "some here have long doubted him."
reports.postmortemNote: The meeting happened, logged and innocent. WREN's last line is its faction talking.

tellLabels.access-mismatch: The reporter couldn't have known this
tellLabels.conditional-gift: The gift comes with a condition
tellLabels.fishing: Asks us to show our hand
tellLabels.only-public-dates: Matches only what anyone could look up
tellLabels.leak-origin: Only the other side could have leaked it
tellLabels.agenda-aligned: Lines up with the reporter's own agenda
tellLabels.wrong-channel: Wrong net and precedence for this kind of order
tellLabels.too-on-message: Says exactly what the adversary wants you to hear

endings.title: Burned
endings.text: Elsin arrests Vell on the morning of the vote. Six months later the ledger is shown to be a forgery built from his public schedule. Kalsa stops taking allied intelligence at its word. Kordav got everything it sent LANTERN for.

endings.title: Sidelined
endings.text: The caveated warning leaks within a day and is quoted in the opposition's speech. Vell resigns "to clear his name." Elsin's reformers lose their strongest voice.

endings.title: Exposed
endings.text: Elsin's defence minister stands up in parliament with your warning: Kordav is running a smear, and its "defector" was sent. The motion fails by forty votes. LANTERN's statement is never released. Two Bureau officers are recalled from Aubrec, and this time it is real.

endings.title: Survived
endings.text: Your warning reaches Kalsa the night before the vote. The motion fails by three. Vell keeps his job, and the allegation follows him.

endings.title: Shelved
endings.text: Nothing left the building. The opposition runs with the MP's claim anyway, and Vell survives by five votes. He never learns how close it was, or who was behind it.

dailyUpdates.text: Elsin's parliament will vote on a no-confidence motion against Deputy Defence Minister Aron Vell on the 12th.
Debriefing continues. Elsin's opposition steps up its attacks on Vell.
The no-confidence vote has been moved up to the 10th.
Elsin's coalition partners say they'll decide how to vote "on the evidence." The vote is the day after tomorrow.

script.text: LANTERN arrived with a gift and a condition. The gift was IRON HARVEST: all of it true, and worth nothing to Kordav, because the operation had been known for three months. The condition was resettlement before details. He said the Vell allegation came from "colleagues in the Bureau." A planning officer doesn't see the Bureau's agent files.

If you pressed him for details, he gave you room 412. The Kalsa Courier had printed it three weeks before he walked in. His question about who could vouch for him was his second task: to find out who we have in the ministry. And if you were reading the Bureau's headquarters net, you saw a recall that never happened. Kordav put it where it believed we were listening.
The ledger was genuine paper carrying a forged story. Every payment fell on a trip anyone could look up, and none on a trip Vell hadn't announced.
The deadline he pressed was the vote, and only Kordav needed the allegation to land before it. The MP's word "defected" could only have come from LANTERN's side.

Kordav said nothing about a missing officer for four days, then announced a kidnapping on the eve of the vote. The same day, the kidnapped man asked to record a press statement. Through all of it the Bureau's office in Aubrec changed nothing.

lessons: True details show access. They say nothing about intent. LANTERN's account of IRON HARVEST was accurate and cost Kordav nothing.
Check a claim against access. A General Staff planner had no way to see Bureau agent files.
Count where a detail comes from. Room 412 had been in a newspaper for three weeks.
Watch how the other side reacts, on every channel you can reach. A service that has really lost an officer changes its codes and questions his family. The Bureau did neither.
The adversary knows some of what you collect. The recall was sent on the net Kordav believed we read.
Asking can be seen. The Bureau was watching the ministry for anyone who asked about LANTERN.

missedCollection.1: The Bureau's office in Aubrec (SIGINT) or LANTERN's family (OSINT): either shows that Kordav isn't doing any damage control.
missedCollection.2: Elsin's press (OSINT, 1 point): the newspaper story that "room 412" came from.
missedCollection.3: Questioning LANTERN on the ledger: he can't explain how a planner got into the Bureau's registry.
missedCollection.4: Anything still untasked on Kordav's reaction. It's the last tasking that can arrive before the vote.
missedCollection.5: Nothing tasked today could arrive in time.

postmortem.openQuestion: The Bureau put its staged recall on the one net it believed we were reading. It was right. What made it believe that?

pirs.question: Is LANTERN who he says he is, with the access he claims?
How is Kordav reacting to his disappearance?
Where does the allegation against Vell come from?

targets.name: Question LANTERN: his access
targets.fallback: The session on this went over old ground. Nothing new.

targets.name: Question LANTERN: the Vell details
targets.fallback: The session on this went over old ground. Nothing new.

targets.name: Question LANTERN: his family
targets.fallback: The session on this went over old ground. Nothing new.

targets.fallback: The session on this went over old ground. Nothing new.

targets.name: FINCH, inside Kordav's defence ministry
targets.fallback: No meeting with FINCH could be arranged in time.

collection.note: Questioning LANTERN is HUMINT at 2 points. A meeting with FINCH costs 3 and takes two days.

burnRules.text: FINCH didn't come to the meeting. His signal site has not been serviced.
burnRules.readIn: FINCH has reported, and has since missed his safety signal.
burnRules.postmortem: The Bureau was watching the ministry for whoever came asking about LANTERN, which is what LANTERN's question on Day 2 was for. FINCH's meeting was seen. The ministry's public directory would have answered the same question for 1 point.

levels.label: Trusted
levels.text: She acts on your confidence as given, with your full collection budget.

levels.label: Questioned
levels.text: Her office trims your collection: 1 point less a day.

levels.label: Discounted
levels.text: 2 points less a day, and she treats your confidence as one step lower: High gets the Medium action, Medium the Low one.

triggers.rule: A warning she sent on your word is rebuffed
triggers.note: Credibility −2. She called an ally's witness a liar on your word after one interview, and Kalsa shut the door.

triggers.rule: She has to withdraw a warning she passed on your word
triggers.note: Credibility −1. She had to withdraw the caveated warning she passed on your assessment.

triggers.rule: She has to withdraw a smear warning
triggers.note: Credibility −1. She had to take back a warning to an ally.

triggers.rule: Low confidence two days running (each further Low day too)
triggers.note: Credibility −1. Low again. "I can't take 'perhaps' to a minister twice."

credibility.summary: Marlowe can't see whether you're right until it's over. She can see when she has to take something back, and when you won't commit.

map.title: Schematic of the three capitals
map.caption: Three capitals, not to scale. Reporting will be plotted here as it arrives.
map.truthNote: Red diamonds are what the Bureau was really doing on Day {day}.
map.legend: Plots reporting as it arrives, not confirmed fact. Dashed pins are items you doubted. Dashed rings are today's taskings.

analysts.name: Imre Vasko
analysts.reveal: He settles on a reading early. He began well, with the vote. Then LANTERN's IRON HARVEST details persuaded him the man was genuine, and nothing afterwards moved him.

analysts.name: Noor Halden
analysts.reveal: Careful, and slow. Her notes come a day after the item. She wasn't wrong once, and each time you had already briefed without her.

notes.text: The vote is the only story in Kalsa this week. Whatever arrives before it will be used against Vell, whoever sent it.
Calm proves nothing. Staff officers rehearse everything. And what he gave us on IRON HARVEST was right to the hour. I think he's real.
notes.why: The details were true and cost Kordav nothing. He anchored on them.

notes.text: That is real Bureau paper. A man inventing a story for a visa doesn't get hold of it.
notes.why: Right that he's no lone fabricator. Wrong about what follows: the Bureau gave it to him.

notes.text: He's asking about his family now because it has sunk in that he isn't going home. That's normal by the fourth day.
notes.why: On Day 1 she would 'be fine.' The story changed when the pressure did.

notes.text: So Kordav has noticed he's gone. This is how a real defection looks from the other side: silence, then outrage.
notes.why: Four days of silence, then a kidnapping story on the eve of the vote.

notes.text: I checked what he gave us on IRON HARVEST against our own file. We already held all of it. It's accurate, and none of it is new.
The dates are all public trips. If I were paying an agent, I'd do it on the trips nobody could look up.
notes.why: The ledger's flaw, a day after the analysis.

notes.text: We told nobody. Elsin's service had talk of "someone from Kordav," nothing about a defector. So where did the MP get the word "defected"?
notes.why: The leak could only have come from LANTERN's side.

notes.text: A recall after a compromise goes out on the operational channel at the highest precedence. This went on the admin net, routine, with the officers named. I think it was meant to be read.
notes.why: The staged recall, caught on procedure. A day late if you'd already briefed on it.

notes.text: An exact room number, and he can't say how he knows it. That usually comes from a briefing or a newspaper.

caseFile.text: You checked the Bureau's own office traffic, or doubted the recall: the headquarters net carried a message meant for us.
